newsitem.title: CANADA: GOLF-DUDLEY HART WINS CANADIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUDLEY HART WINS CANADIAN OPEN.

text.p: Fiery Dudley Hart kept his renowned temper under control as he compiled a bogey-free final round to win the rain-shortened Bell Canadian Open by one stroke on Sunday.
Hart made just two birdies, but he scrambled well to card a closing two-under-par 70 in a blustery breeze at Glen Abbey for his first tour victory.
He sank his winning putt from three feet at the par-five 18th to edge out fellow American David Duval.
Hart finished at 14-under 202 in the event shortened to 54 holes because of Saturday's heavy rain.
Duval's 68 equalled the day's lowest round, but a birdie at the last was not enough and he finished runner-up for the fifth time on the PGA Tour, where he still has not won.
Tour rookie Scott Dunlap, who started the final round with a three-shot lead, faded with a 76 to tie for third, three shots off the pace.
"I'm really proud of myself because I have been a little volatile in the past," said Hart, 28, who became the 10th first-time winner on the PGA Tour this year.
"I'm the baby volcano," he continued. "I've always had a temper. I've worked really hard on it (and) I did a good job today.
"I had a lot of scrambling on the back side. I managed to get up and down from some tough places."
Hart collected $270,000 to jump to 51st on this year's money list. He also became the first player since Peter Oosterhuis in 1981 to record his first tour victory at the Canadian Open.
Duval claimed he was not disappointed, despite another near-miss: "It's hard for me to be disappointed when I shot four under in a national championship on a difficult course," he said.
"I've played well enough to win several tournaments. There's nothing you can do about another player."
Tiger Woods, playing his second tournament as a professional, matched Duval's closing 68th to finish 11th, his best result in 19 professional events.
Woods played 17 professional events on the U.S. and European Tours during his amateur days. His best result had been equal 22nd at this year's British Open.
He turned professional two weeks ago after winning his third successive U.S. amateur title, and tied for 60th in his pro debut in Milwaukee last week.
"I scrambled like hell the first two days, but today I played really well," said Woods, who missed just two fairways.
He will be the star attraction at the Quad Cities Classic starting Thursday.
